intent.raw_query: Tokyo city break, $3000 for couple, food and tech culture, April 2026 from SFO

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the famous Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from local vendors. This self-guided or small-group tour immerses you in Tokyo's vibrant food culture and is ideal for late morning arrival days when you want a low-key but rewarding first experience close to central hotels.

experiences.name: Akihabara Tech and Anime District Walk
experiences.description: Dive into Tokyo's legendary electronics and pop culture hub. Visit multi-floor gadget stores, retro game shops, maid cafes, and cutting-edge tech showrooms. This is the epicenter of Japan's tech culture and is easily accessible from most central Tokyo hotels, making it perfect for an afternoon or evening outing.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Asakusa Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, Senso-ji, and stroll through the historic Nakamise shopping street. Experience traditional ceremonies, incense rituals, and local craft shopping. Asakusa is centrally located and pairs well with nearby Tsukiji, making it easy to combine both in one day without long commutes.

experiences.name: Shibuya Ramen and Izakaya Evening Experience
experiences.description: Spend an evening exploring Shibuya's dense network of ramen shops and traditional izakayas. Try regional ramen styles such as tonkotsu and shoyu, and enjoy small plates with local sake or craft beer. Shibuya is a central hub with excellent transport links, minimizing travel time from most recommended hotel zones.

experiences.name: teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the world-renowned teamLab Borderless digital art experience, a fusion of technology, art, and culture unique to Tokyo. The new Azabudai Hills venue is centrally located and easily reachable from Roppongi or Shibuya area hotels, making it a convenient full-afternoon activity that perfectly blends tech culture with artistic immersion.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Tokyo, Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 13:00. Use morning for in-flight rest and preparation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Narita or Haneda Airport at 13:00. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage. Take the budget-friendly Airport Limousine Bus or Narita Express (N'EX) to Chiyoda City. Check in to Chiyoda City Boutique Stay. Freshen up and take a relaxed orientation walk around the Imperial Palace East Gardens — free entry, stunning traditional landscaping.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Hibiya Park nearby, then explore the Yurakucho area for your first taste of Tokyo nightlife. Duck under the train tracks to find Yurakucho Gado-shita — a row of tiny izakayas (Japanese gastropubs) under the elevated railway, perfect for cheap yakitori skewers and cold Asahi beer.

meals.breakfast: In-flight meal
meals.lunch: Airport convenience store bento box (Lawson or 7-Eleven inside the airport) — approx. ¥600–¥900
meals.dinner: Yurakucho Gado-shita izakaya — yakitori skewers, edamame, and draft beer for approx. ¥1,500–¥2,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Get a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport — it works on all trains, subways, and even convenience store purchases. Buy a 24/72-hour Tokyo Metro pass if you plan heavy subway use. April is cherry blossom season — the Imperial Palace area may still have late blooms!

day_by_day.morning: Start with a free morning walk around the Imperial Palace moat — a beloved jogging and sightseeing route. Visit Nijubashi Bridge for iconic photos. Head to nearby Kitanomaru Park, which is free and often beautiful in spring. Visit the National Museum of Modern Art (MOMAT) — entry is only ¥500 for the permanent collection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short metro ride to Akihabara — Tokyo's legendary Electric Town. Explore multi-story electronics shops like Yodobashi Akiba, retro game shops, anime merchandise stores, and maid cafes. Browse the free floors of Yodobashi and Don Quijote for tech and gadget culture immersion. Visit the free Akihabara Radio Kaikan building for retro electronics and hobby culture.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Akihabara for dinner. Explore the basement and upper floors of department stores for affordable set meals. Then visit a retro arcade (game center) — budget ¥500–¥1,000 for games. Experience the neon-lit streets of Akihabara at night for a quintessential Tokyo tech-culture atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby convenience store onigiri + coffee — approx. ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Ramen at a local Akihabara ramen shop — try Ichiran or a local alternative for approx. ¥900–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Yoshinoya or Matsuya beef bowl chain near Akihabara for a filling meal — approx. ¥500–¥700, or a set meal at a local teishoku restaurant for ¥800–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best explored slowly — budget 4–5 hours. Many shops don't open until 10:00–11:00 AM. Free Wi-Fi available at many electronics shops. Look for discount bins in game shops for budget retro gaming souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Asakusa, Tokyo's most traditional district. Visit Senso-ji Temple — Tokyo's oldest and most iconic temple, completely free to enter. Explore Nakamise-dori shopping street for traditional snacks and souvenirs. Try ningyo-yaki (small cakes shaped like figures) fresh from street stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Sumida River and cross to the other side for views of Tokyo Skytree (viewing deck is pricey — admire it from the base for free). Explore the Sumida area and the free Sumida Park. Return to Asakusa and visit Kappabashi Kitchenware Street — a fascinating street full of professional cooking equipment and the famous plastic food display models. Free to browse!
day_by_day.evening: Take the Tokyo Metro to Ueno for evening exploration. Walk through Ueno Park (free), which may still have late cherry blossoms. Explore Ameya-Yokocho (Ameyoko) Market — a bustling open-air market street with cheap street food, fresh fish, clothing, and snacks. Great for budget dinner grazing.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel — approx. ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Asakusa street food: try melonpan, ningyo-yaki, and yakitori sticks from Nakamise-dori stalls — approx. ¥500–¥800
meals.dinner: Ameyoko Market food stalls — gyoza, takoyaki, fresh sushi, or a sit-down ramen shop nearby — approx. ¥800–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is open 24 hours but the main hall opens at 6:00 AM. Arrive early to avoid crowds. Kappabashi is closed on Sundays. Ameyoko is liveliest in the evening — great for people-watching and budget eats.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to Harajuku. Visit Meiji Jingu Shrine — one of Tokyo's most serene Shinto shrines set in a forested area. Free entry. Walk the long forested path to the main shrine for a peaceful morning. Explore the nearby Yoyogi Park, especially lively on weekends with street performers, picnickers, and local clubs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down Takeshita Street (Takeshita-dori) in Harajuku — the epicenter of Tokyo youth fashion and pop culture. Browse quirky fashion boutiques, crepe stands, and kawaii shops. Then walk to Omotesando for window shopping along Tokyo's Champs-Élysées. Explore the backstreets (Ura-Harajuku) for independent vintage and design shops.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya — a short walk or one metro stop from Harajuku. Watch the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing at rush hour (most impressive 18:00–20:00). Visit the free observation deck at Shibuya Scramble Square (lower floors) or view the crossing from the Starbucks overlooking it (buy a cheap drink for the view). Explore Shibuya Center-gai for street food and atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or bakery near Harajuku station — approx. ¥300–¥600
meals.lunch: Harajuku crepe from Marion Crepes or Angel's Heart — approx. ¥600–¥800, plus takoyaki or street snacks
meals.dinner: Shibuya food court in Shibuya Hikarie or Shibuya 109 basement — various options from ¥800–¥1,500, or a gyudon (beef bowl) at Sukiya near the scramble

day_by_day.notes: Weekends in Harajuku and Shibuya are very crowded — go early to Meiji Shrine. The Shibuya Scramble is best photographed from elevated positions. Look for the Hachiko statue outside Shibuya Station — a famous Tokyo landmark.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Yanaka — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old neighborhoods that survived WWII bombing. Explore Yanaka Ginza, a charming traditional shotengai (shopping street) with local vendors, snacks, and crafts. Visit Yanaka Cemetery, which is beautiful in spring and culturally significant. Browse the narrow alleyways for a glimpse of old Shitamachi (downtown) Tokyo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Nezu Shrine — a lesser-known but stunning shrine with hundreds of torii gates (similar to Kyoto's Fushimi Inari but far less crowded). Free entry. Then visit the nearby Tokyo National Museum in Ueno — the largest museum in Japan. Entry is ¥1,000 and includes extensive collections of Japanese art, samurai armor, and cultural artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ueno or head to Akihabara for a relaxed evening. Try a conveyor belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) restaurant for a fun and budget-friendly dinner. Kura Sushi or Hamazushi offer plates from ¥110–¥165 each. End the evening with a walk through a covered shotengai (shopping arcade) near your hotel.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka Ginza street food — freshly made melon bread or croquette from local shops — approx. ¥200–¥400
meals.lunch: Local teishoku set meal restaurant in Yanaka or Nezu area — approx. ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Kaiten-zushi (conveyor belt sushi) near Ueno or Akihabara — approx. ¥1,000–¥1,500 for a satisfying meal

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is perfect for slow, unhurried exploration. Many small shops are family-run and cash-only. The Tokyo National Museum is closed on Mondays — Sunday is a great day to visit. Nezu Shrine's azalea festival may be ongoing in April.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic artificial island in Tokyo Bay. Start with a free walk along the Odaiba seaside promenade with views of the Rainbow Bridge and Tokyo skyline. Visit the teamLab Borderless or Planets digital art museum (book in advance — approx. ¥3,200). If budget is tight, admire the exterior architecture of Fuji TV Building and the giant Gundam statue for free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore DiverCity Tokyo Plaza — free to browse, home to the life-size Gundam RX-78 statue. Visit the free floors of Palette Town or Aqua City Odaiba mall. Head to the free Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation) lobby exhibits, or pay ¥630 for the full museum — excellent for tech culture enthusiasts featuring ASIMO robot demos and space exploration exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Take the Yurikamome automated driverless monorail back toward central Tokyo — the ride itself is a futuristic experience. Stop at Shimbashi for dinner. Explore the izakayas and standing bars (tachinomi) around Shimbashi Station — a beloved salaryman district with very affordable food and drinks.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — approx. ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Food court at DiverCity Tokyo Plaza or Aqua City Odaiba — ramen, curry, or soba for approx. ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Shimbashi izakaya or standing soba/ramen bar — approx. ¥1,000–¥1,500 including drinks

day_by_day.notes: The Yurikamome monorail offers great views — sit in the front car for the best perspective. Miraikan is closed on Tuesdays. teamLab requires advance booking — check availability and pricing before your trip.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (approx. 2 hours from Asakusa via Tobu Nikko Line — budget option approx. ¥1,360 one way). Arrive in Nikko and head to the UNESCO World Heritage Tosho-gu Shrine complex — one of Japan's most ornate and historically significant shrine complexes. Entry approx. ¥1,300. See the famous 'See No Evil, Hear No Evil, Speak No Evil' monkeys carving.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the surrounding Rinno-ji Temple and Futarasan Shrine (combo tickets available). Walk the cedar-lined Omotesando approach. If time allows, hike up to Taiyuin Mausoleum — slightly less crowded and equally impressive. Enjoy the mountain forest atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening (depart Nikko by 16:00–17:00). Arrive back in Chiyoda area by 18:30–19:00. Have a relaxed dinner near the hotel. Use the evening to do laundry, plan remaining days, and rest.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast before catching the train — approx. ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Nikko yuba (tofu skin) cuisine — a local specialty. Try a yuba soba set at a local restaurant near the shrines — approx. ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.dinner: Convenience store bento or nearby ramen/curry shop near hotel — approx. ¥700–¥1,000

day_by_day.notes: Take the Tobu Nikko Line from Asakusa (not JR) for the most budget-friendly option. The Tobu 'Nikko All Area Pass' (approx. ¥4,780) covers round-trip train and local buses — good value. Wear comfortable walking shoes as the terrain is hilly.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Jimbocho — Tokyo's famous used bookstore district, just a short walk from Chiyoda. Browse dozens of second-hand bookshops, vintage map dealers, and print shops. Even if you don't read Japanese, the atmosphere is unique and many shops have English books and vintage art prints. Completely free to browse.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Akihabara for a deeper tech culture dive. Visit the Akihabara Radio Center and Radio Kaikan for vintage electronics and components. Explore the free floors of Sofmap and Bic Camera. Visit Super Potato — a legendary retro video game store with games from Famicom to PlayStation era. Then head to the nearby 3331 Arts Chiyoda — a free contemporary art space in a converted school building.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Kanda Myojin Shrine — one of Tokyo's oldest shrines and interestingly the patron shrine of IT companies in Akihabara. Free entry, beautifully lit in the evening. Then explore the local izakayas around Kanda Station for dinner — a working-class neighborhood with very affordable food.

meals.breakfast: Local kissaten (traditional Japanese coffee shop) near Jimbocho — coffee and toast set (morning service) for approx. ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Kanda curry — Kanda is famous for its curry restaurants. Try one of the many affordable curry shops for approx. ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Kanda izakaya — yakitori, tofu dishes, and beer for approx. ¥1,200–¥1,800

day_by_day.notes: Jimbocho is best visited on weekday mornings when it's less crowded. Many bookshops have outdoor bargain bins with items for ¥100–¥200. Kanda Myojin has a fascinating connection to anime and gaming culture — look for the ema (votive plaques) dedicated by tech companies.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to Shinjuku. Start at the free Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck (opens 9:30 AM) for panoramic 360-degree views of Tokyo — completely free and one of the best views in the city, including Mt. Fuji on clear days. Then explore Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (entry ¥500) — one of Japan's most beautiful parks, especially in spring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Shinjuku's various neighborhoods. Visit Kabukicho — Tokyo's famous entertainment district, fascinating to explore in daylight. Walk through the Golden Gai — a maze of tiny atmospheric bars (best visited at night). Explore Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane / Piss Alley) — a narrow alley of tiny yakitori stalls under the train tracks near the west exit.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Shinjuku at night — one of Tokyo's most electric evening atmospheres. Visit Golden Gai for a drink at a tiny themed bar (most have a cover charge of ¥500–¥1,000 but drinks are reasonably priced). Alternatively, have dinner at Omoide Yokocho for grilled yakitori in an atmospheric setting. Explore the neon-lit streets of east Shinjuku.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel — approx. ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Shinjuku Takashimaya Times Square basement food hall — pick up prepared foods, sushi, or bento — approx. ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho yakitori — approx. ¥1,500–¥2,000 for a full meal with drinks in the atmospheric alley

day_by_day.notes: The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building has two towers — the South Tower is sometimes closed for maintenance. Check the schedule online. Shinjuku Gyoen prohibits alcohol — it's a peaceful contrast to the busy city. Golden Gai bars are very small (some seat only 6–8 people) — be respectful and adventurous.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kamakura (approx. 1 hour from Shinjuku via JR Shonan-Shinjuku Line — approx. ¥920 one way). Visit the Great Buddha (Kotoku-in) — a 13-meter bronze Buddha statue, one of Japan's most iconic landmarks. Entry ¥300. You can go inside the statue for an extra ¥20.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kamakura's temple trail. Visit Hase-dera Temple (entry ¥400) for beautiful gardens and ocean views. Walk the Daibutsu Hiking Course through forested hills connecting multiple temples — free trail. Visit Tsurugaoka Hachimangu Shrine — the spiritual center of Kamakura, free entry. Browse Komachi-dori shopping street for local snacks and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Stop in Yokohama's Chinatown (Chukagai) on the way back for a cheap and delicious dinner — one of the largest Chinatowns in the world with hundreds of restaurants. Then return to Chiyoda for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel or convenience store breakfast — approx. ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Kamakura local food — try shirasu (whitebait) rice bowl or soba at a local restaurant on Komachi-dori — approx. ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.dinner: Yokohama Chinatown — dim sum, Peking duck, or a set menu at a mid-range Chinese restaurant — approx. ¥1,200–¥2,000

day_by_day.notes: Kamakura is very popular on weekends — a Friday visit means smaller crowds. Wear comfortable shoes for the hiking course. The JR Pass does NOT cover the Enoden Line within Kamakura — buy a separate ticket or day pass (¥660) if you want to use it.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tsukiji Outer Market (the inner wholesale market moved to Toyosu, but the outer market remains). Arrive early (8:00–9:00 AM) for the best experience. Browse fresh seafood stalls, street food vendors, and kitchen supply shops. Try a fresh tuna sashimi breakfast, tamagoyaki (egg omelet) on a stick, and freshly grilled scallops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Ginza — Tokyo's most upscale shopping district. Window shop at flagship stores of luxury brands (all free to browse). Visit the free Itoya stationery flagship store — a fascinating 12-story stationery and art supply store. Explore the free galleries in Ginza — many art galleries offer free admission. Visit the Kabuki-za Theatre exterior and browse the souvenir shop inside.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shiodome or Shimbashi for dinner. Visit the Caretta Shiodome building for a free illumination display (seasonal) and a view of the Tokyo skyline. Explore the affordable restaurants in the basement of Caretta. Alternatively, head back to Yurakucho for another round of izakaya dining under the tracks.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh sashimi, tamagoyaki, and grilled seafood — budget ¥1,000–¥1,500 for a grazing breakfast
meals.lunch: Ginza department store basement (depachika) — pick up prepared foods, sushi, and snacks — approx. ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Yurakucho izakaya or Shiodome food court — approx. ¥1,200–¥1,800

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market gets very crowded by 10:00 AM on weekends — arrive early. Most stalls are cash-only. Ginza on a Saturday afternoon closes Chuo-dori street to traffic (pedestrian paradise from 15:00) — great for strolling.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum in Ryogoku (entry ¥600) — an excellent museum covering Tokyo's history from the Edo period to the modern era, with life-size reconstructions of old Tokyo streets and buildings. Fascinating for understanding the city's cultural evolution.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Ryogoku Kokugikan (Sumo Arena). If a sumo tournament is running in April (the Spring Basho is in March, so check if any exhibition matches are scheduled), try to get tickets (from ¥2,200 for upper seats). Otherwise, visit the free Sumo Museum inside the arena and watch practice sessions at nearby sumo stables (Arashio Stable allows free observation from the street in the mornings). Explore the chanko-nabe restaurants in the area — the hearty stew eaten by sumo wrestlers.
day_by_day.evening: Take the metro to Roppongi for evening culture. Visit the free outdoor sculpture garden at Roppongi Hills (open until late). Explore the streets of Roppongi — Tokyo's international nightlife district. Have dinner at one of the many affordable international restaurants. Visit a jazz bar or live music venue for a cultural evening (cover charges typically ¥1,000–¥2,000).

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — approx. ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Chanko-nabe set meal in Ryogoku — the sumo wrestlers' hearty hot pot stew, available at local restaurants for approx. ¥1,200–¥1,800
meals.dinner: Roppongi international restaurant or izakaya — approx. ¥1,200–¥1,800

day_by_day.notes: The Edo-Tokyo Museum is one of Tokyo's best value museums — allow 2–3 hours. Sumo stable practice (asageiko) typically runs 6:00–10:00 AM — adjust morning plans if interested. Roppongi is safe but busy on Sunday evenings — stay aware of your surroundings.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning walk around the Imperial Palace moat for a peaceful farewell to Chiyoda. Visit the Kitanomaru Park and the Science Museum (Kagakukan) if not visited — entry ¥830, excellent for tech culture enthusiasts with hands-on science exhibits. Alternatively, revisit a favorite neighborhood for any last purchases or photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at Akihabara (electronics, anime goods) or Asakusa (traditional crafts). Visit a 100-yen shop (Daiso, Seria, or Can Do) for affordable quality souvenirs — many items are genuinely useful and uniquely Japanese. Pack bags and check out of hotel. Store luggage at the hotel or at a coin locker (¥300–¥500) at the nearest station.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner at a special Tokyo restaurant — treat yourself slightly. Try a tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet) set meal at Maisen or a similar restaurant — approx. ¥1,500–¥2,000 for a quality meal. Head to the airport via Airport Limousine Bus or train. Depart Tokyo with wonderful memories.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a sit-down kissaten (Japanese coffee shop) morning set — coffee, toast, egg, and salad for approx. ¥500–¥700
meals.lunch: 100-yen sushi (Kura Sushi or Hamazushi) for a fun final budget lunch — approx. ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.dinner: Slightly splurge farewell dinner — tonkatsu, tempura, or sushi set at a quality local restaurant — approx. ¥1,500–¥2,500

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for airport travel and check-in. Narita Airport is 60–90 minutes from central Tokyo; Haneda is 30–45 minutes. Return or top up your Suica/Pasmo card balance at any station — remaining balance can be refunded (¥220 handling fee). Pack any purchased electronics carefully to avoid customs issues.

trip_options.title: Classic Tokyo, Japan Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Use the time on board to rest and prepare.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Narita or Haneda Airport at 13:00. Clear customs and immigration, then take the Narita Express (N'EX) or Limousine Bus to Chiyoda City. Check in to your boutique hotel, freshen up, and take a gentle orientation stroll around the Imperial Palace East Gardens — a serene green space just minutes from Chiyoda. Enjoy the spring cherry blossoms if they are still blooming in mid-April.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Kanda or Jimbocho neighborhood (a short walk or subway ride from Chiyoda) for your first Tokyo dinner. Explore the lively backstreets and settle in for the night early to beat jet lag.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a bento box or onigiri from a convenience store (7-Eleven or Lawson) near the airport or station — a quintessential Tokyo experience (¥500–¥800)
meals.dinner: Kanda Yabu Soba — a historic soba restaurant near Chiyoda serving handmade buckwheat noodles in a traditional setting (¥1,200–¥2,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for seamless subway and convenience store payments. Download Google Maps and the Tokyo Metro app. April mid-month may still have late cherry blossoms — check Sakura forecast.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a peaceful morning walk around the Imperial Palace moat — a beloved 5 km jogging and strolling route with stunning views of the palace walls and gardens. Visit the Nijubashi Bridge for iconic photos. Explore the East Gardens when they open at 9:00 AM (free entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Akihabara Electric Town (10 minutes by subway from Chiyoda) — Tokyo's legendary tech and otaku culture hub. Browse multi-story electronics shops like Yodobashi Camera and BIC Camera, explore retro game shops, anime merchandise stores, and maid cafes. Visit the Akihabara Radio Center for vintage electronics and components.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Akihabara for dinner and evening exploration. Visit a multi-floor arcade (Game Center) like Taito Station for an authentic Tokyo gaming experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby kissaten (old-school Japanese coffee shop) — try a morning set (toast, egg, coffee) for ¥500–¥800
meals.lunch: Akihabara ramen at Fuunji-style tsukemen shop or a curry rice spot in the area (¥900–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Kanda Matsuya — another celebrated soba institution near Akihabara, or try a yakiniku (grilled meat) restaurant in Akihabara for ¥2,000–¥3,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best experienced on a weekday when it is less crowded. Many electronics shops open around 10:00–11:00 AM. Maid cafes typically charge a table fee plus drink minimum — budget ¥1,000–¥2,000 for the experience.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Asakusa — Tokyo's most atmospheric old downtown district. Visit Senso-ji Temple (Tokyo's oldest temple) early morning before crowds arrive. Walk through the Nakamise shopping street for traditional souvenirs, snacks, and crafts. Explore the Asakusa Shrine adjacent to the temple.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Sumida River and cross to the Tokyo Skytree (world's second tallest tower). Purchase tickets for the Tembo Deck (350m) for panoramic views of Tokyo. Explore the Solamachi shopping complex at the base for local food products and design goods.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Asakusa for the vibrant evening atmosphere. Explore the Hoppy Street (Hoppy-dori) area for casual izakaya dining and local street life.

meals.breakfast: Grab freshly made ningyo-yaki (small cakes) and a matcha from a Nakamise stall for a street breakfast (¥300–¥600)
meals.lunch: Asakusa Imahan — a classic sukiyaki and shabu-shabu restaurant near Senso-ji with a mid-range lunch set (¥1,500–¥2,500), or try tempura at Daikokuya Tempura (¥1,500–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Hoppy Street izakaya — order yakitori, edamame, and cold Hoppy (barley-based drink) at an outdoor table for a very local experience (¥2,000–¥3,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free to enter and open 24 hours, but the main hall opens at 6:00 AM. Tokyo Skytree tickets: Tembo Deck costs ¥2,100 on weekdays. Book in advance online to skip queues. The Sumida River area is beautiful in spring with riverside cherry trees.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ueno — home to one of Tokyo's greatest cultural clusters. Spend the morning at the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno Park, Japan's oldest and largest museum housing incredible collections of samurai armor, ukiyo-e prints, ceramics, and Buddhist art (¥1,000 entry). Stroll through Ueno Park, a beloved public green space.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Yanaka — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) neighborhoods, a short walk from Ueno. Wander through Yanaka Ginza shopping street, browse independent craft shops, and explore the serene Yanaka Cemetery with its old temple atmosphere and seasonal flowers.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Akihabara or Ochanomizu (both near Chiyoda) for a tech-focused evening. Visit the Ochanomizu musical instrument district or return to Akihabara for evening shopping, which stays lively until 21:00–22:00.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a bakery near the hotel — Tokyo has excellent French-Japanese fusion bakeries (¥600–¥1,000)
meals.lunch: Yanaka Ginza street food — try menchi katsu (fried meat cutlet), croquettes, and local snacks from the various small shops (¥800–¥1,200 total)
meals.dinner: Ueno Yabu Soba or try a Korean-Japanese fusion restaurant in the Ueno-Okachimachi area, which has a vibrant Korean food scene (¥1,500–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday means Ueno Park will be busy — arrive at the museum when it opens at 9:30 AM. Yanaka is a wonderful off-the-beaten-path area that most tourists miss. The neighborhood has a very authentic, unhurried Tokyo feel.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Harajuku. Visit Meiji Jingu Shrine — a grand Shinto shrine set in a forested 70-hectare park, offering a peaceful contrast to the city. Arrive early (opens at sunrise) to see morning worshippers and possibly a traditional wedding ceremony.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down Takeshita Street in Harajuku for Tokyo's famous youth fashion and pop culture scene — crepe stands, quirky fashion boutiques, and colorful streetwear. Then shift to the nearby Omotesando boulevard — Tokyo's most elegant shopping street — for upscale boutiques, architecture by world-famous designers, and people-watching at open-air cafes.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya (10 minutes walk from Harajuku). Experience the iconic Shibuya Scramble Crossing — best viewed from the Starbucks or Mag's Park overlooking the intersection. Explore the Shibuya Center-gai and surrounding streets.

meals.breakfast: Eggs 'n Things Harajuku or a local kissaten for a relaxed Sunday morning breakfast (¥800–¥1,500)
meals.lunch: Harajuku crepe from Marion Crepes (¥600–¥900) followed by a sit-down lunch at a trendy Omotesando cafe — try bills Omotesando for brunch (¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.dinner: Shibuya — try Ichiran Ramen (solo ramen booths, a unique Tokyo experience) or Gyukatsu Motomura (beef cutlet restaurant) for ¥1,200–¥2,000

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is free to enter. Sunday mornings often feature traditional Shinto wedding processions — a beautiful cultural sight. Harajuku Takeshita Street gets very crowded on Sundays — go early or be prepared for the crowds as part of the experience.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic artificial island in Tokyo Bay. Take the driverless Yurikamome monorail from Shimbashi for scenic bay views. Visit teamLab Planets or teamLab Borderless (book tickets well in advance) — world-renowned immersive digital art museums that perfectly blend tech culture and art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Odaiba: visit the life-size Unicorn Gundam statue at DiverCity Tokyo Plaza, browse the Toyota Mega Web (interactive automotive showroom, free), and enjoy the waterfront promenade with views of the Rainbow Bridge and a replica Statue of Liberty.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Tokyo. Head to the Ginza district (close to Chiyoda) for a sophisticated evening stroll along Japan's most famous luxury shopping street. Window shop the flagship stores and explore the free observation decks at Itoya stationery store.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a convenience store breakfast before heading to Odaiba (¥500–¥800)
meals.lunch: Odaiba Decks Tokyo Beach food court — try fresh seafood, ramen, or Japanese-style hamburgers with bay views (¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Ginza area — try Kyubey (if budget allows, ¥4,000–¥6,000 for a sushi lunch set is more affordable than dinner) or opt for a more casual tonkatsu restaurant like Ginza Bairin (¥1,500–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: teamLab tickets MUST be booked online in advance — they sell out weeks ahead. Prices are approximately ¥3,200 per person. The Yurikamome monorail ride itself is a scenic experience worth enjoying slowly. Odaiba can be combined with a late afternoon sunset over Tokyo Bay.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge day — sleep in slightly. Take a slow morning walk through the Imperial Palace outer grounds and Kitanomaru Park (adjacent to the palace). Visit the National Museum of Modern Art, Tokyo (MOMAT) in Kitanomaru Park — excellent collection of 20th-century Japanese art (¥500 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Jimbocho — the world's largest concentration of used and antiquarian bookshops, just minutes from Chiyoda. Browse hundreds of specialty bookstores for vintage manga, ukiyo-e prints, old maps, academic texts, and rare Japanese books. Even non-readers will enjoy the atmosphere and visual culture.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Kanda and Ochanomizu area for dinner. This neighborhood has excellent curry restaurants — Tokyo's curry culture is deeply tied to the student and tech community historically centered here.

meals.breakfast: Late hotel breakfast or a neighborhood bakery (¥600–¥1,000)
meals.lunch: Jimbocho area — try Bondy, a famous European-style curry restaurant beloved by Tokyo's intellectual community since 1973 (¥1,500–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Kanda neighborhood izakaya — try a small local place for yakitori and cold beer, a perfect mid-trip unwind (¥2,000–¥3,000)

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate slower-paced day to avoid burnout mid-trip. Jimbocho is a unique cultural experience unlike anything outside Japan — even if you cannot read Japanese, the visual culture of the shops is fascinating. Many shops are closed on Sundays, so Monday or Tuesday is ideal.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko — a UNESCO World Heritage Site approximately 2 hours from Chiyoda by Tobu Nikko Line from Asakusa. Depart by 8:00 AM to maximize time. Visit the extraordinarily ornate Tosho-gu Shrine complex, dedicated to Tokugawa Ieyasu, founder of the Edo shogunate. The shrine is decorated with thousands of intricate carvings and gold leaf.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko: walk to Rinno-ji Temple, the Yomeimon Gate (one of Japan's most spectacular gates), and the peaceful Futarasan Shrine. If time allows, take a bus or taxi to Kegon Falls — one of Japan's most famous waterfalls, especially dramatic in spring.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by 19:00–20:00. Enjoy a simple, relaxing dinner near the hotel after the day trip.

meals.breakfast: Grab an onigiri and coffee from a convenience store near Asakusa station before the early train (¥400–¥700)
meals.lunch: Nikko Yuba (tofu skin) cuisine — a local Nikko specialty. Try Gyoshintei restaurant near the shrines for a traditional yuba lunch set (¥2,000–¥3,000)
meals.dinner: Simple ramen or soba near Chiyoda hotel — something comforting after a full day of walking (¥900–¥1,500)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Nikko All Area Pass at Asakusa Tobu Station (approximately ¥4,780 round trip including unlimited buses in Nikko). Tosho-gu entry is ¥1,300. Wear comfortable walking shoes — the shrine complex involves significant uphill walking on stone paths. Start early to beat tour groups.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shinjuku — Tokyo's busiest and most layered district. Start at the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building (free observation deck open from 9:00 AM) for panoramic city views including Mt. Fuji on clear days. Explore the surrounding West Shinjuku skyscraper district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross to East Shinjuku. Explore Kabukicho — Tokyo's famous entertainment district (interesting to walk through even in daylight). Visit the Golden Gai — a remarkable cluster of around 200 tiny bars in a preserved alleyway network, fascinating to explore in the afternoon. Browse Shinjuku's many department stores including Isetan and Takashimaya.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Shinjuku for dinner and evening entertainment. Experience the Golden Gai at night — each tiny bar holds only 5–10 people and has a unique theme. Choose one that appeals to you and have a drink with locals.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Shinjuku Takashimaya's basement food hall (depachika) for pastries and coffee (¥700–¥1,200)
meals.lunch: Shinjuku Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — a narrow alley of tiny yakitori stalls near the west exit. Order skewers and beer at a standing counter (¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Shinjuku Tsunahachi — a beloved tempura restaurant chain with excellent quality and reasonable prices (¥2,000–¥3,500), or explore the restaurant floors of Takashimaya Times Square

day_by_day.notes: The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck is free and offers one of the best city views. On clear April days, Mt. Fuji is often visible in the morning before haze builds. Golden Gai bars typically have a small cover charge (¥500–¥1,000) but are a truly unique Tokyo experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shibuya for a deeper exploration. Start at the Shibuya Sky observation deck on top of Shibuya Scramble Square — a rooftop outdoor observation experience with 360-degree views (¥2,000, book online). Then visit Shibuya Stream and the surrounding tech startup district — this area around Shibuya has become Tokyo's Silicon Valley equivalent.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Daikanyama and Nakameguro — two of Tokyo's most stylish and design-forward neighborhoods, a short walk from Shibuya. Visit the Daikanyama T-Site (Tsutaya Books) — an architecturally stunning bookshop and lifestyle complex beloved by Tokyo's creative class. Walk along the Meguro River canal.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Shibuya or head to nearby Ebisu for dinner in a lively Friday evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Log Road Daikanyama area cafe or a Shibuya cafe breakfast (¥800–¥1,500)
meals.lunch: Nakameguro — try a trendy ramen shop or a Japanese-Italian fusion restaurant along the canal (¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Ebisu — try Ebisu Yokocho (a covered alley of small izakaya and specialty restaurants) for a lively Friday night dinner with locals (¥2,500–¥3,500)

day_by_day.notes: Shibuya Sky tickets should be booked online in advance, especially for Friday. Daikanyama T-Site is open until 26:00 (2 AM) and is a remarkable place to browse even late at night. The Meguro River in April may still have some late-blooming cherry trees creating a beautiful tunnel effect.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tsukiji Outer Market — the world's most famous fish market area, still operating as a retail and restaurant hub after the inner wholesale market moved to Toyosu. Arrive by 8:00 AM to experience the morning rush. Browse fresh seafood, pickles, knives, and cookware stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Toyosu Market (the new wholesale market) — take a guided viewing tour of the tuna auction area (book in advance through the Tokyo Metropolitan Central Wholesale Market website). Then visit teamLab Planets in Toyosu if not already visited on Day 6. Alternatively, explore the Kiyosumi-Shirakawa neighborhood — Tokyo's specialty coffee capital, home to Blue Bottle Coffee Japan's first location and dozens of independent roasters.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Roppongi for the evening — Tokyo's international arts and nightlife district. Visit Mori Art Museum (open until 22:00 on Fridays and Saturdays) on the 53rd floor of Roppongi Hills, which includes a city view observatory.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast — fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (egg roll), grilled scallops, and uni (sea urchin) on rice from market stalls (¥1,500–¥2,500 for a full market breakfast spread)
meals.lunch: Kiyosumi-Shirakawa — specialty coffee and a light lunch at a third-wave coffee roaster cafe (¥1,200–¥1,800)
meals.dinner: Roppongi — try a mid-range Japanese restaurant in Roppongi Hills or Azabu area, such as a yakitori restaurant or modern Japanese cuisine (¥3,000–¥4,500)

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji is best on weekdays but Saturday mornings are still excellent — arrive early as the best items sell out by 10:00 AM. Mori Art Museum entry (¥1,800) includes the Tokyo City View observatory. The museum often hosts world-class contemporary art exhibitions.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hamarikyu Gardens — a beautiful traditional Japanese garden at the mouth of the Sumida River, adjacent to Chiyoda (very close to your hotel). The garden features tidal ponds, teahouses, and seasonal flowers. Take a traditional matcha tea ceremony at the garden's teahouse overlooking the water (¥300 for tea, ¥300 garden entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Sumida River water bus from Hamarikyu to Asakusa for a scenic river journey (¥1,020, approximately 40 minutes). Revisit Asakusa with fresh eyes — explore the Kappabashi Kitchenware Street (just north of Asakusa) — a fascinating wholesale district selling professional kitchen equipment, realistic plastic food models, and Japanese tableware.
day_by_day.evening: Final major evening in Tokyo — celebrate with a special dinner. Head back toward Ginza or Chiyoda for a memorable meal. Consider a conveyor belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) at a higher-end establishment for a fun yet quality experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — take time to enjoy it on this penultimate full day (included or ¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.lunch: Asakusa area — try Sometaro, a famous okonomiyaki (savory pancake) restaurant where you cook at your own table (¥1,500–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Ginza Sushi Ichi or Uobei Sushi in Shibuya (touch-panel ordering conveyor sushi, excellent quality at ¥150–¥300 per plate) — a fun and memorable final dinner (¥2,000–¥4,000 depending on choice)

day_by_day.notes: Hamarikyu Gardens are open Tuesday–Sunday (closed Mondays). The water bus to Asakusa is a wonderful way to see Tokyo from the water — book at the Hamarikyu pier. Kappabashi Street is a unique shopping experience — the plastic food display models make excellent and very Japanese souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — pack and check out of the hotel (standard checkout is 11:00 AM). Store luggage at the hotel or a coin locker. Take a final slow walk through the Imperial Palace outer gardens one last time for a peaceful farewell to Chiyoda.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute shopping and souvenir run. Head to the Marunouchi/Tokyo Station area (walking distance from Chiyoda). Explore the Tokyo Station Ichibangai and the GRANSTA shopping complex inside Tokyo Station — excellent for high-quality Japanese food souvenirs, wagashi (traditional sweets), sake, and snacks. Pick up ekiben (station bento boxes) as a final Tokyo food experience.
day_by_day.evening: Depart for the airport based on your flight schedule. Allow at least 2–3 hours before departure for check-in and security at Narita (90 min by N'EX from Tokyo Station) or Haneda (30–40 min by monorail or subway).

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or a nearby kissaten for a nostalgic last Tokyo morning coffee and toast (¥600–¥1,000)
meals.lunch: Tokyo Station GRANSTA food hall — graze on various Japanese specialties: tamagoyaki, croquettes, sushi rolls, and matcha desserts (¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or ekiben (train station bento) purchased at Tokyo Station to enjoy on the Narita Express (¥1,200–¥2,000)

day_by_day.notes: Leave ample time for airport transfer — Narita Airport requires at least 90 minutes travel time from central Tokyo. The N'EX (Narita Express) from Tokyo Station is the most reliable option. Use remaining Suica card balance at convenience stores or vending machines — you can also refund the remaining balance at the airport before departure (minus a ¥220 handling fee).

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Tokyo, Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the famous Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from local vendors. This self-guided or small-group tour immerses you in Tokyo's vibrant food culture and is ideal for late morning arrival days when you want a low-key but rewarding first experience close to central hotels.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Narita/Haneda Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from airport to Chiyoda City Boutique Stay. Settle into your suite, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome amenity prepared by the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation stroll around the Imperial Palace East Gardens (Higashi Gyoen), just minutes from Chiyoda City. Admire the historic stone walls, serene Japanese gardens in full spring bloom, and the iconic Fushimi Yagura watchtower. A peaceful introduction to Tokyo without overwhelming jet-lagged senses.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a refined kaiseki restaurant in Chiyoda — Kanda (1-michelin-star) or Kohaku for an exquisite multi-course Japanese haute cuisine experience. Afterwards, a quiet nightcap at the hotel bar to acclimate to the time zone.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or at airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Light bento or ramen at a quality spot near the hotel after check-in — try Kyushu Jangara Ramen in Akihabara (10-min walk)
meals.dinner: Kaiseki dinner at Kanda or Kohaku — expect 12–16 artfully crafted seasonal courses with sake pairing (¥30,000–¥50,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Request an early check-in through the hotel in advance. Carry yen cash for small purchases. Pick up a Suica card at the airport for seamless transit throughout the trip. April in Tokyo means cherry blossom season — pack layers as evenings can be cool (12–18°C).

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — Join a premium guided tour of the iconic Tsukiji Outer Market. Sample ultra-fresh nigiri sushi, handmade tamagoyaki (rolled omelette), uni on rice, wagyu skewers, and seasonal street snacks from legendary vendors. A sensory feast and a deep dive into Tokyo's culinary soul.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Ginza for a curated luxury shopping and cultural experience. Visit the Itoya flagship stationery store (a design lover's paradise), browse the Hermès Maison Ginza or Mikimoto Pearl boutique, and stop into the Ginza Six rooftop garden for panoramic city views. Explore the Chanel Nexus Hall for cutting-edge art exhibitions.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Sukiyabashi Jiro Honten (Ginza) or Sushi Saito — world-class omakase sushi in an intimate 10-seat counter setting. Book months in advance. Alternatively, dine at Ginza Kojyu for contemporary kaiseki with impeccable seasonal ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a premium coffee and pastry at Café de l'Ambre, Tokyo's legendary kissaten (coffee house) near Ginza
meals.lunch: Tsukiji Market grazing — curated bites across 6–8 vendors during the food tour (included in tour)
meals.dinner: Omakase sushi at Sukiyabashi Jiro or Sushi Saito — 20-course experience (¥40,000–¥80,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Tsukiji food tour should be booked with a premium operator (e.g., Arigato Japan Food Tours or a private guide). Wear comfortable walking shoes. Ginza shops open around 11:00. Reserve sushi dinner months ahead — concierge assistance strongly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Akihabara Electric Town — Tokyo's legendary tech and electronics district, just a short walk or train ride from Chiyoda. Explore multi-story electronics megastores like Yodobashi Akiba and BIC Camera, browse rare retro gaming shops, visit the Gundam Café, and discover the latest in robotics, VR gadgets, and cutting-edge consumer tech.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to teamLab Borderless (or teamLab Planets in Toyosu) for an immersive digital art experience — one of the world's most celebrated tech-meets-art installations. Spend 2–3 hours wandering through interactive light forests, mirrored infinity rooms, and AI-driven art environments that blur the line between technology and nature.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the Marunouchi or Nihonbashi district — try Narisawa for innovative 'Innovative Satoyama Cuisine' blending Japanese tradition with avant-garde technique, or dine at Florilège for boundary-pushing French-Japanese fusion. Both are among Tokyo's most celebrated fine dining destinations.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — request a traditional Japanese set (gohan, miso soup, grilled fish, pickles, tamago)
meals.lunch: Akihabara lunch at Kanda Yabu Soba — a historic, refined soba restaurant near Akihabara serving handmade buckwheat noodles in elegant surroundings since 1880
meals.dinner: Narisawa or Florilège — 10–12 course tasting menu with wine pairing (¥35,000–¥60,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book teamLab tickets online well in advance — timed entry is required. Akihabara is best explored on foot. Many electronics stores have tax-free counters for foreign visitors — bring your passport. Check if teamLab Borderless has reopened at its new Azabudai Hills location by 2027.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Imperial Palace surroundings and Kitanomaru Park — starting from your doorstep in Chiyoda. Walk along the palace moat lined with weeping cherry trees (late bloomers may still be visible in mid-April), visit the Nippon Budokan exterior, and explore the Science Museum or National Museum of Modern Art (MOMAT) in Kitanomaru Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Yanaka — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) neighborhoods. Wander Yanaka Ginza shopping street for artisan crafts, traditional sweets, and local snacks. Visit Yanaka Cemetery, a hauntingly beautiful cherry blossom spot. Browse independent galleries and ceramics studios tucked into narrow alleyways.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Tokyo for a sky-high cocktail experience at the Andaz Tokyo Rooftop Bar (Toranomon Hills) or the Park Hyatt New York Bar (made famous by Lost in Translation). Dinner at RyuGin — a legendary 3-Michelin-star restaurant celebrating Japanese seasonal cuisine with theatrical precision.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or artisan coffee and toast at Fuglen Tokyo (Tomigaya) — a beloved Norwegian-Japanese café
meals.lunch: Yanaka neighborhood lunch — handmade soba at Nezu no Taiya or a traditional lunch set at a local izakaya
meals.dinner: RyuGin (3 Michelin stars) — seasonal kaiseki with extraordinary ingredient sourcing and presentation (¥50,000–¥70,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes. Saturday means crowds at popular spots; arrive early. The MOMAT has an excellent permanent collection of 20th-century Japanese art. Book RyuGin at least 2–3 months ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Harajuku and Omotesando morning — visit the serene Meiji Jingu Shrine set within a forested sanctuary in the heart of the city. Participate in a traditional Shinto ritual (temizuya purification, torii gate walk). Explore the tranquil inner garden if open. A meditative counterpoint to Tokyo's urban energy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll down Omotesando — Tokyo's most elegant boulevard — browsing flagship architecture by Tadao Ando (Omotesando Hills), Herzog & de Meuron (Prada), and Toyo Ito (Tod's). Visit the Nezu Museum for a world-class collection of Asian antiquities set in a bamboo garden. Browse concept boutiques and design galleries in the Minami-Aoyama backstreets.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Aoyama or Minami-Aoyama — try L'Effervescence for soulful French cuisine rooted in Japanese ingredients, or Quintessence for minimalist, ingredient-driven fine dining. Both are Michelin-starred and beloved by Tokyo's culinary cognoscenti.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel before heading out early for the shrine visit
meals.lunch: Lunch at Omotesando Hills or a premium café — try Anniversaire Café for elegant French-style brunch with terrace seating overlooking the boulevard
meals.dinner: L'Effervescence or Quintessence — 8–12 course tasting menu (¥30,000–¥55,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Shrine is most peaceful early morning — aim to arrive by 9:00. Sunday brings local crowds to Harajuku's Takeshita Street (skip unless curious about youth fashion). The Nezu Museum garden café is a lovely afternoon rest stop. Book dinner well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private sake brewery tour and tasting in the greater Tokyo area — arrange a premium experience at a traditional sake kura (brewery) such as Ozawa Shuzo in Ome (90 min from central Tokyo) or a curated sake education session with a certified kikizake-shi (sake sommelier) at a premium sake bar in Ginza or Nihonbashi.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Nihonbashi — Tokyo's historic commercial and cultural heart. Explore the Mitsui Memorial Museum (Japanese art and decorative arts), browse Coredo Muromachi for premium Japanese lifestyle brands, and visit the Nihonbashi Mitsukoshi flagship department store — Japan's oldest department store with exceptional food halls and artisan goods.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Sazenka — a legendary Michelin-starred Chinese restaurant in Hiroo helmed by Chef Tomoya Kawada, blending authentic Chinese technique with premium Japanese ingredients. One of Tokyo's most exclusive and reservations-coveted dining experiences.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at Nihonbashi Yukari (3 Michelin stars) — refined kaiseki-inspired Japanese cuisine in a historic setting
meals.dinner: Sazenka — 10-course Chinese kaiseki with rare tea pairing (¥40,000–¥70,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The sake experience can be arranged through a specialist tour operator or your hotel concierge. Nihonbashi Mitsukoshi's basement food hall (depachika) is a must-visit for premium Japanese confections, wagashi, and gourmet ingredients. Sazenka requires reservations months in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko — a UNESCO World Heritage site approximately 2 hours from Tokyo by Tobu Limited Express. Explore the breathtaking Toshogu Shrine complex, a lavishly decorated 17th-century mausoleum surrounded by ancient cedar forests. Visit Rinnoji Temple and the serene Shinkyo Sacred Bridge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko — walk to Kegon Falls (one of Japan's most spectacular waterfalls), stroll along Lake Chuzenji if time permits, and browse Nikko's artisan shops for lacquerware and traditional crafts. Enjoy the mountain air and natural scenery as a refreshing contrast to urban Tokyo.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by late afternoon. Unwind with a private onsen (hot spring bath) experience arranged at a premium Tokyo hotel spa (The Peninsula, Aman Tokyo, or Four Seasons). Dinner at a neighborhood yakitori restaurant in Yurakucho under the train tracks — Birdland is the gold standard for premium yakitori with Binchotan charcoal-grilled chicken.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departing for Nikko
meals.lunch: Traditional Japanese lunch at Nikko Kanaya Hotel — Japan's oldest resort hotel, serving classic Western-Japanese fusion cuisine since 1873 in a historic setting
meals.dinner: Birdland Yakitori (Yurakucho) — premium charcoal-grilled chicken omakase with sake pairing (¥20,000–¥35,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Nikko World Heritage Pass at Asakusa Tobu Station for unlimited transport and shrine entry. Wear comfortable walking shoes — significant walking on uneven stone paths. Return trains run until late evening. Birdland requires advance reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Mori Art Museum and Tokyo City View observation deck in Roppongi Hills — one of Tokyo's finest contemporary art institutions with panoramic 360-degree views of the city skyline. Explore the current exhibition (internationally curated, always world-class). Walk through the Roppongi Hills complex and its public art installations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the National Art Center Tokyo in Roppongi — Japan's largest exhibition space with rotating world-class exhibitions. Visit 21_21 Design Sight in Midtown Tokyo (designed by Tadao Ando) for cutting-edge design and art exhibitions. Browse the Suntory Museum of Art for traditional Japanese decorative arts.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Azabu Kadowaki — an intimate, highly acclaimed kaiseki restaurant in Azabu-Juban known for its extraordinary seasonal ingredients and the legendary truffle rice course. One of Tokyo's most coveted dinner reservations.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a premium morning set at a Roppongi Hills café
meals.lunch: Lunch at the National Art Center's Brasserie Paul Bocuse Le Musée — a stunning Paul Bocuse-branded restaurant inside the museum building with French cuisine and a spectacular interior
meals.dinner: Azabu Kadowaki — intimate kaiseki with legendary truffle rice course (¥40,000–¥60,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Mori Art Museum is open late (until 22:00 most nights) — the observation deck at night offers spectacular views. Book Kadowaki months in advance through your hotel concierge. Roppongi is walkable between Roppongi Hills and Midtown.

day_by_day.morning: Private hands-on Japanese cooking class with a professional chef in Tokyo — learn to prepare dashi from scratch, nigiri sushi, miso soup, and a seasonal side dish. Classes offered by premium operators like Hattori Nutrition College, Tsukiji Cooking, or a private chef experience arranged through the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Koenji and Shimokitazawa — Tokyo's bohemian, creative neighborhoods beloved for vintage fashion, independent record stores, live music venues, and artisan coffee. Browse rare vinyl at Flash Disc Ranch, discover curated vintage clothing, and soak in the alternative cultural energy that contrasts with Chiyoda's imperial formality.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Shinjuku — visit Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane), a narrow atmospheric alleyway of tiny yakitori stalls under lantern light, for a quintessential old-Tokyo experience. Follow with drinks at a premium whisky bar — Bar Benfiddich (Shinjuku) is world-renowned for its artisanal cocktails using rare Japanese botanicals and house-distilled spirits.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before the cooking class
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the cooking class — most premium cooking experiences include a full sit-down meal of your creations
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho yakitori stalls (casual, atmospheric — ¥3,000–¥6,000 per person) followed by premium whisky/cocktails at Bar Benfiddich

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class at least 2 weeks in advance. Shimokitazawa is best explored on foot — the neighborhood is compact and pedestrian-friendly. Omoide Yokocho is cash-only and very small — arrive by 18:00 to secure a spot. Bar Benfiddich requires reservations.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa — Tokyo's oldest and most iconic temple. Arrive early (before 8:30) to experience the spiritual atmosphere before tour groups arrive. Walk the Nakamise-dori shopping street for traditional crafts, ningyo-yaki cakes, and washi paper goods. Explore the backstreets of Asakusa for artisan workshops producing traditional Japanese goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sumida Hokusai Museum — a stunning contemporary building by Kazuyo Sejima housing the world's finest collection of Hokusai woodblock prints. Cross the Azuma Bridge for views of the Tokyo Skytree. Ascend the Tokyo Skytree (634m) to the Tembo Galleria for extraordinary panoramic views — book the premium Tembo Galleria floor for the highest vantage point.
day_by_day.evening: Private river cruise on the Sumida River at sunset — arrange a premium yakatabune (traditional Japanese houseboat) dinner cruise with kaiseki cuisine, sake, and views of illuminated bridges and the Tokyo skyline. A uniquely romantic and culturally immersive evening experience.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Japanese breakfast at a historic Asakusa establishment — Asakusa Imahan for sukiyaki-style morning set, or Daikokuya Tempura for early tempura
meals.lunch: Lunch at Sometaro — a beloved old-school okonomiyaki restaurant in Asakusa where you cook your own savory pancakes at the table
meals.dinner: Yakatabune dinner cruise on the Sumida River — premium kaiseki and sake aboard a traditional houseboat (¥25,000–¥45,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the yakatabune cruise well in advance through operators like Yakatabune Harumiya or Funayado Mikawaya. Tokyo Skytree Tembo Galleria tickets can be booked online. The Hokusai Museum is small but extraordinary — allow 90 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Private visit to a traditional Japanese tea ceremony at a premium venue — Urasenke Tea School (Tokyo branch) or a private tea house in Hamarikyu Gardens. Learn the philosophy of wabi-sabi, practice temae (tea preparation ritual), and enjoy matcha and wagashi in an authentic tatami setting with a certified tea master.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Daikanyama and Nakameguro — Tokyo's most stylish and sophisticated neighborhoods. Browse the iconic Daikanyama T-Site (a stunning bookstore-lifestyle complex designed around a forest). Walk along the Meguro River lined with late-blooming sakura trees and independent boutiques. Visit Cow Books for rare Japanese publications.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Den — one of Tokyo's most celebrated and creative restaurants, serving playful yet deeply rooted Japanese cuisine. Chef Zaiyu Hasegawa's tasting menu is a joyful, surprising journey through Japanese flavors with unexpected modern twists. A truly memorable culinary experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch in Daikanyama — Log Road Daikanyama complex or a premium sandwich and coffee at Ivy Place (a beloved neighborhood restaurant with garden terrace)
meals.dinner: Den (Jimbocho) — creative Japanese tasting menu with theatrical presentation (¥25,000–¥40,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the tea ceremony experience through your hotel concierge or directly with Urasenke Tokyo. Nakameguro is particularly beautiful if any cherry blossoms remain along the canal. Den is one of Asia's 50 Best Restaurants — book months in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Hakone — Japan's premier onsen resort region, approximately 90 minutes from Tokyo by Romancecar (luxury express train from Shinjuku). Check into a premium ryokan (Japanese inn) for a day-use onsen experience — Gora Kadan or Hakone Hoshi no Akari offer exceptional facilities with views of Mt. Fuji.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Hakone's cultural and natural highlights — visit the Hakone Open Air Museum (Japan's first outdoor sculpture museum featuring Picasso, Moore, and Rodin alongside Mt. Fuji views), take the Hakone Ropeway over volcanic Owakudani valley with sulfurous steam vents, and cruise Lake Ashi on a replica pirate ship for iconic Fuji views (weather permitting).
day_by_day.evening: Ryokan kaiseki dinner at Gora Kadan or Hakone Hoshi no Akari — a multi-course feast of Hakone and Kanagawa seasonal ingredients served in your private tatami room or an intimate dining hall. Soak in the open-air rotenburo (outdoor hot spring bath) under the stars before dinner. Return to Tokyo by late evening Romancecar.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departing for Hakone
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Hakone Open Air Museum café or a local soba restaurant near Gora Station
meals.dinner: Ryokan kaiseki at Gora Kadan or Hakone Hoshi no Akari — 10–12 course seasonal dinner with sake pairing (¥35,000–¥60,000 per person, day-use package)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Hakone Free Pass at Shinjuku for unlimited transport throughout the Hakone area. Mt. Fuji visibility is weather-dependent — morning views are most reliable. Book the day-use ryokan package well in advance. The Romancecar observation car offers stunning scenery — book premium seats.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Chiyoda — a reflective walk around the Imperial Palace outer gardens and moat, appreciating the city one last time. Visit the Kitte building (a beautifully converted historic post office) opposite Tokyo Station for premium Japanese artisan goods and souvenirs — Biken-do for wagashi, Nakagawa Masashichi Shoten for crafts, and premium sake and tea shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute luxury shopping and gift procurement — Mitsukoshi Ginza or Takashimaya for premium Japanese confections, wagyu gifts, rare whisky, and artisan crafts. Visit Itoya Ginza for exquisite stationery and gifts. Enjoy a final matcha parfait or kakigori (premium shaved ice) at a renowned Ginza café.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Joël Robuchon Tokyo (Ebisu) — the legendary French master's Tokyo outpost offering the ultimate in European fine dining with Japanese precision and ingredients. Alternatively, end with a sentimental return to your favorite restaurant from the trip. Private luxury transfer to the airport for departure.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — request a special send-off from the kitchen
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at Kitte Marunouchi — Hamacho Kaneko for refined Japanese cuisine or Ukai-tei Ginza for premium teppanyaki with wagyu
meals.dinner: Joël Robuchon Tokyo (Ebisu Garden Place) — legendary French haute cuisine tasting menu with sommelier wine pairing (¥50,000–¥80,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for airport transfer and check-in. Request a late checkout from the hotel if your flight departs in the evening. Pack any purchased food items (wagashi, tea, sake) in checked luggage per customs regulations. Carry receipts for tax-free purchases for airport customs declaration.
